## Highlights

This release stops a SysAP reboot from flooding consumers, such as the Home Assistant integration, with phantom callbacks.

### Reboot replay suppression (#294)

After a reboot, the SysAP replays every datapoint over the WebSocket, one device at a time, over about 25 seconds. The previous 3-second priming window only covered the start of this replay, so the rest reached callbacks as phantom button presses and events.

Priming is now tracked per datapoint. After each WebSocket (re)connect, only the **first** delivery of each datapoint is treated as replay. Replayed values still update the cached state, and they still notify callbacks if the value actually changed. Every later delivery is handled as a live event, including repeated identical presses. The window is now 60 seconds (`WS_PRIMING_SECONDS`), but it only acts as a safety cap.

Within 60 seconds of a reconnect, a live press is suppressed only if it matches the cached value and arrives before that datapoint has been replayed.

Behavior is unchanged when priming is disabled with `FreeAtHomeApi(..., enable_priming=False)`. The `is_priming` property also behaves as before. No code changes are needed, since `FreeAtHome.ws_listen()` applies the new handling automatically.
